subtype: Approach: checking the bag against a short list at the door [Thinking]
passage:
Before the first bell in Class 5, Farida opened her diary and copied five words on the last page: homework, lunch, bottle, pencil box, diary. Thomas, at the next desk, leaned over. "You never forget anything."
"I do when I'm in a hurry," Farida said. "Yesterday Ammi was calling me for the bus and my head went empty. I left my bottle on the table."
"So the list is for the door?"
"Yes. My memory is bad at that time, but a pencil tick doesn't panic. I'll check each thing, one by one." She underlined homework twice. Thomas laughed and copied the idea for himself.

qa.q: What five things did Farida write on the last page of her diary?
qa.a: She wrote homework, lunch, bottle, pencil box and diary.

qa.q: What is Farida worried about when she is in a hurry?
qa.a: She worries that her head goes empty when she is rushed, like the day she left her bottle on the table.

qa.q: What other approach could help Farida, and why?
qa.a: Farida could read the timetable and pack the night before, because a calm evening check leaves less to remember in the morning rush. Keeping things in fixed places could also help.

qa.q: How does Thomas see Farida's list?
qa.a: Thomas finds it sensible enough to copy for himself, so to him it looks like a useful trick and not a weakness.

grounding: A girl writes a short list of five school items and ticks it at the door because she cannot trust her memory when rushed.

subtype: Approach: checking the bag against a short list at the door [Thinking]
passage: I stay with my cousin Payal's family, so I see her mornings. Taped inside the front door, at her eye level, is a list in her round handwriting: homework, diary, lunch, bottle, pencil box. Every morning, just before she steps out, she stops and taps each word, then touches the thing in her bag. Once I asked why she bothers. She said, 'When I'm in a hurry my brain says I packed it, and my brain lies.' Last week Tarun, her little brother, was yelling for his shoe and the van was honking. Payal still stopped. Tap, tap, tap. Bottle, missing. She ran back for it. I can't say whether she was nervous, but she didn't look it.

qa.a: Inside the front door, at her eye level.

qa.q: Why does Payal tap each word even when the van is honking?
qa.a: She knows her memory 'lies' when she's in a hurry, so she seems determined and calm, trusting the list over the feeling of having packed.

qa.q: What else could Payal add to her list, and why?
qa.a: Things that change by day, like PT shoes, since the same check at the door would catch them.

qa.q: What might mornings be like for Tarun compared with Payal?
qa.a: Tarun is yelling for a shoe while the van honks, so his mornings seem much more rushed than Payal's calm tapping.

grounding: Shows a girl checking her bag against a five-item list at the door each morning because her memory is unreliable in a hurry.

subtype: Approach: checking the bag against a short list at the door [Thinking]
passage:
Monday. Binita was sure she had packed her homework. In class it wasn't there. Elizabeth Ma'am wrote a note in her diary. "But I remember putting it in," Binita said, her face hot.
Tuesday. At home Binita sat and thought. When I'm rushing, I only think I remember. So she wrote a list on a card: homework, diary, lunch, bottle, pencil box. Five things. She stuck it on the door.
Thursday. The van horn blew. Binita stopped at the door and ticked the card, one, two, three... no diary. It was on the sofa. She grabbed it and ran. That afternoon, Elizabeth Ma'am's note went back signed.

qa.q: What was missing when Binita ticked the card on Thursday?
qa.a: Her diary; it was on the sofa.

qa.q: How did Binita feel on Monday when the homework wasn't there?
qa.a: Her face was hot, so she felt embarrassed and confused, sure she had packed it.

qa.q: Why does a written list work better than memory for Binita?
qa.a: She worked out that in a rush she only thinks she remembers; the card doesn't forget, so it caught the missing diary.

qa.q: How might Elizabeth Ma'am see the change by Thursday?
qa.a: After writing a note on Monday, Elizabeth Ma'am gets it back signed, which shows Binita is now keeping track.

grounding: Illustrates a girl realising her memory fails when she hurries and using a five-item list at the door to check her bag.
